KEY FINDINGS
Agencies pursuing or defending congestion pricing should proactively pair it
with targeted equity interventions in neighborhoods showing weaker adaptation,
not just tout aggregate ridership gains.
When planning transit-desert remediation under tight-to-moderate budgets,
sequential belief-updating investment plans outperform static optimization by
a meaningful margin (~5-10 points) — agencies should consider phased, data-
For immigrant-heavy service areas, invest in reducing transit access time
(last-mile connections, feeder frequency) rather than fare discounts — it's
roughly three times more effective at sustaining transit mode share.
PAPER OF THE DAY
T-REX: Fast and Dynamic Journey Planning for Continental-
Scale Public Transit Networks
Jonas Sauer, Patrick Steil, Sascha Witt
T-REX applies multi-level overlay partitioning to Trip-Based Transit Routing, pruning
irrelevant local transfers to answer Pareto-optimal journey queries on a full European
transit network in under 10 milliseconds — a 20-80x speedup over prior algorithms — while
Why it matters: Continental-scale, real-time journey planning is a genuine hard computer-science

ACTIONABLE TAKEAWAYS
Agencies pursuing or defending congestion pricing should proactively pair it with
targeted equity interventions in neighborhoods showing weaker adaptation, not just tout
aggregate ridership gains.
When planning transit-desert remediation under tight-to-moderate budgets, sequential
belief-updating investment plans outperform static optimization by a meaningful margin
(~5-10 points) — agencies should consider phased, data-updating rollouts over one-shot
For immigrant-heavy service areas, invest in reducing transit access time (last-mile
connections, feeder frequency) rather than fare discounts — it's roughly three times
more effective at sustaining transit mode share.
GTFS-consuming tools and agencies should consider adopting the DayTypes abstraction to
simplify schedule-change detection and vehicle scheduling rather than re-deriving
recurring patterns ad hoc.
